{"summary":"Architecture memo — recommendation: build a macOS 13+ LSUIElement utility using an AppKit-owned NSStatusItem and NSMenu, with SwiftUI limited to Settings/About. NSStatusItem is the boring, robust choice: it gives explicit lifetime, menu rebuilding, target/action handling, accessibility, and status-button control. MenuBarExtra is simpler, but Apple documents that a menu-only app may terminate if its extra is removed. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsstatusitem and https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/menubarextra

Architecture: keep WorkspaceID, WorkspaceSnapshot, lifecycle state, command results, and transition rules in a Foundation-only domain module. Put process execution and status collection behind an MSWClient actor; expose state through an @MainActor AppModel; let StatusMenuController only render snapshots and dispatch typed intents. Inject CommandRunning, WorkspaceOpening, NotificationSending, LoginItemManaging, and Clock protocols.

CLI boundary: use `msw start|stop|restart WORKSPACE` for every mutation so the app preserves the repository’s Keychain, quarantine, readiness, validation, and timeout behavior. The current `msw status` is human-formatted, so never scrape it. The verified underlying query `msb status -a --label msw.managed=true --format json` returns a JSON array containing name, status, CPU, memory, image, and ports. The preferred integration contract is a future minimal `msw status --format json` pass-through; until then, direct `msb` JSON access is acceptable only for read-only monitoring. Decode with Codable, tolerate additional fields, map unknown statuses explicitly, and treat missing expected workspaces as unavailable rather than stopped.

Execution and environment: resolve the executable in this order: saved explicit path, `~/.local/bin/msw` installed by setup.sh, then known PATH directories. Resolve `~` with FileManager, verify regular executable files, and run `msw version` as a health check. Build a deterministic PATH including the executable directory, `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, and system directories. Never use `sh -c`, `zsh -lc`, source shell profiles, parse config.sh, or concatenate user input into shell text. Pass every workspace, path, port, and scheme as a separate Process argument. Capture stdout and stderr concurrently with bounded buffers, preserve exit code and termination reason, redact logs, and never log the environment. Foundation Process inherits its launcher’s environment: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/process

Polling and concurrency: lifecycle status has no suitable stable event stream; `metrics --watch` is unrelated and should not drive VM state. Use a single-flight adaptive poll: approximately 2 seconds while the menu is open or a transition is pending, 10 seconds while idle, plus immediate refresh at launch, menu opening, wake, and command completion. Observe wake through NSWorkspace’s notification center. Preserve the last good snapshot and mark it stale after failures. Serialize mutations per workspace in an actor, disable conflicting actions, and represent starting/stopping optimistically without claiming success before a confirming poll. Tasks belong to the application model, not menu views, so closing the menu does not cancel a VM operation. Cancel polling promptly; normally let lifecycle mutations finish. If enforcing hard timeouts, terminate and reap the Process, then kill after a grace period; use a process-group runner if descendant termination must be guaranteed. Source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsworkspace/didwakenotification

Launch at login: use SMAppService.mainApp.register/unregister, surface enabled, notRegistered, requiresApproval, and notFound states, and link to Login Items settings when approval is required. Do not add a helper target or custom LaunchAgent. Register only after the app is installed at a stable path. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/servicemanagement/smappservice/mainapp and https://developer.apple.com/documentation/servicemanagement/smappservice/register()

Sandbox and signing: disable App Sandbox for this personal utility. A sandboxed child inherits restrictions, cannot freely traverse the user’s CLI/config/SSH locations, and NSWorkspace ignores launch arguments from sandboxed callers. A Mac App Store build is therefore a poor fit unless the architecture is replaced by a bundled helper and explicit user-selected resources. Keep Hardened Runtime enabled, sign with Developer ID, notarize and staple direct distributions, and avoid unnecessary exception entitlements. The app itself must never read msw’s GitHub tokens; the existing CLI remains their owner. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/protecting-user-data-with-app-sandbox, https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsworkspace/openconfiguration/arguments, and https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/notarizing-macos-software-before-distribution

Notifications: request UNUserNotificationCenter authorization only from an explicit Settings toggle and install its delegate during launch. Notify only after an initial baseline, for deduplicated meaningful transitions such as an unexpected running-to-stopped change or a user-requested operation failure. Suppress notifications caused by the app’s own stop command. Notification actions should carry validated workspace identifiers and dispatch typed intents; never embed arbitrary commands. Source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/unusernotificationcenter

External opening: centralize app discovery with NSWorkspace and bundle identifiers. For Terminal, open an `ssh://root@WORKSPACE.msb` URL specifically with Terminal; the repository’s SSH ProxyCommand starts a stopped VM, though this path opens the guest home rather than a requested `/workspace` subdirectory. Avoid AppleScript and its Automation permission. For Ghostty, locate `com.mitchellh.ghostty` and launch a new application instance with argument-array semantics equivalent to `-e <resolved-msw> WORKSPACE [PATH]`; local Ghostty help confirms macOS CLI launch should go through app launching. For Zed, execute `msw zed WORKSPACE [PATH]`, preserving its readiness and SSH URI behavior. For browsers, run `msw start WORKSPACE`, obtain the validated URL from `msw url`, validate its scheme/host/port, then call NSWorkspace.open. If an app-specific URL scheme is later added, allow-list actions and workspaces and never accept a raw command. Source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsworkspace

Testability: unit-test JSON fixtures including unknown fields/statuses, missing workspaces, malformed output, stale-state behavior, transition deduplication, polling coalescence, cancellation, timeouts, and per-workspace serialization. Test environment discovery against fake homes and executable paths. Use fake command runners to assert exact executable/argument arrays, including hostile-looking paths that must remain single arguments. Add integration tests with temporary fake `msw` and `msb` executables, plus focused menu-controller tests using injected snapshots. Keep real VM, login-item, notification, browser, and application launching behind opt-in smoke tests.

Verification: inspected README.md, config.sh, bin/msw, setup.sh, command documentation, existing fake-backed tests, installed command help, and read-only JSON status output. Confirmed there is currently no Swift/Xcode app. No files were edited and no project-wide tests, formatters, or linters were run. The working tree’s existing unrelated changes were preserved. Posted the completed design milestone to Gazette: https://gazette.sylve.org/a/msw-guardian/status/1000410","filesChanged":[]}
